rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a new predictive model, while the target paper uses Monte Carlo simulation to induce chemical short-range order. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (computational prediction vs. atomistic simulation of structural change).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions standard thermal-insulation conditions and experimental measurement techniques, whereas the target paper uses atomistic simulation (Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics) under a single-phase bcc constraint. These are different regimes entirely.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis focuses on capturing lattice disorder to predict phonon scattering and mean free paths, while the target paper's mechanism involves SRO reducing lattice distortion and creating percolation pathways that increase conductivity. These are contradictory mechanisms (reducing vs. increasing conductivity).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts identification of alloys with lower phonon thermal conductivity, while the target paper finds that SRO increases lattice heat conductivity by ~12%. These are opposite directions of change.
